scope: Distinct MWCC code-generation behaviors documented in reports/GEDE01/progress.json open_items and docs/matching.md

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical MWCC rotates, swaps, or coalesces overlapping long-lived values across callee-saved GPRs or FPRs differently from retail, even when size, control flow, and relocations otherwise agree.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for every listed function

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical MWCC assigns short-lived volatile integer or floating-point webs to different registers: f1/f4 instead of retail f0/f2, r3 instead of retail r5 for a converted mode, r4/r5 in the opposite roles for a zero/max temporary and current byte, or six different volatile-register choices in a branchless counter update.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for every listed function

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical MWCC materializes, folds, or coalesces object, table, string, or stack-address bases differently from retail, changing temporary registers, indexed-versus-displacement loads, relocation counts, or prologue size.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for every listed function

lessons.precise_divergence: Without a source-level preference, GC/1.3 reuses a branch-dead state register for the replacement-context temporary instead of preserving the retail r27 lifetime, changing four instructions.
lessons.workaround: Declare the replacement-context temporary with the register qualifier.

lessons.precise_divergence: Typing the root at 0x803003C8 as a four-byte pointer holder selects SDA addressing, while retail uses absolute lis/addi references to a non-small-data aggregate.
lessons.workaround: Represent the root as the observed non-small-data aggregate.

lessons.precise_divergence: Combining an object-info lookup with a later halfword assignment lets canonical MWCC shorten the converted s32 value's lifetime and emit a redundant extsh or clrlwi that is absent from retail.
lessons.workaround: Evaluate the lookup separately into the documented typed pointer so the raw s32 remains live across the calls until the direct halfword store.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_8000EC94 and fn_8001BFD0

lessons.precise_divergence: Reusing the script-argument local for the option-switch result lets canonical MWCC eliminate the overwritten first argument's conversion, while retail preserves that value for the later fn_80201814 call.
lessons.workaround: Recover a distinct object_id local so script argument 1 and the option-switch value have separate lifetimes.

lessons.precise_divergence: The branch-disjoint script/object pointer web and fourth value-block field do not receive retail's registers or store schedule when their declarations and assignments are ordered differently.
lessons.workaround: Preserve the documented declaration and assignment order.

lessons.precise_divergence: Implicit unsigned-halfword normalization retains a redundant result move and prevents retail's r28-r31 allocation.
lessons.workaround: Express the normalization as an explicit 0xFFFF mask.

lessons.precise_divergence: Source declaration order controls whether the long-lived lbl_80302400/lbl_8023D020 bases receive retail's r31/r30 assignment.
lessons.workaround: Use the documented declaration order for the two long-lived global bases.

lessons.precise_divergence: Retail retains the global +0x1C fade-subobject pointer in r29, while canonical MWCC folds those accesses into the global root and removes repeated interior-pointer materializations.
A wider node-handle lifetime prevents retail's dedicated r23 allocation and conflicts with the hit result held in r27.
lessons.workaround: Scope the node handle to the branch that owns it.

lessons.precise_divergence: Distinct result variables in the final five construction cases do not recover retail's r31 allocation.
lessons.workaround: Reuse the primary result variable in those five cases.

lessons.precise_divergence: Keeping the spawned object in a distinct local shortens the incoming create-record lifetime and does not reproduce retail's r29 allocation.
lessons.workaround: Reuse the incoming create-record local for the spawned object.

lessons.precise_divergence: GC/1.3 emits the loop-index copy in the loop body, while retail schedules the same copy in the loop latch.
Canonical MWCC schedules the initial constant-vector copy differently around the six callee-saved argument moves.
Equivalent stores, loads, argument setup, or temporary copies occupy a different local scheduling window from retail, sometimes shifting subsequent relocation sites despite matching behavior.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for every listed function

lessons.precise_divergence: An unnecessary volatile qualifier on the local value pair and non-retail low-byte assignment order change the constant schedule and stack-store order.
lessons.workaround: Remove the volatile qualifier and assign the duplicated transformed values' low bytes in retail order.

lessons.precise_divergence: Declaring lbl_80237F38 const changes placement of its vector loads relative to saved-register setup instead of preserving retail's grouped load schedule.
lessons.workaround: Declare lbl_80237F38 as writable Vec3.

lessons.precise_divergence: Ordinary rectangle reads do not preserve retail's prompt-argument scheduling.
lessons.workaround: Use volatile rectangle reads.

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical GC/1.3 emits ten signed-16-bit zero tests as extsh. instructions, while retail uses the equivalent cmpwi form; function size and all text relocations otherwise agree.
Canonical GC/1.3 reverses the operands of one symmetric integer equality comparison; the 244-byte function and all 10 text relocations otherwise agree exactly with retail.
Semantically equivalent conditional source did not reproduce retail's sparse branch tree; expressing the result handling as a switch over -2, -1, 0, and default did.
lessons.workaround: Express the final result handling as the documented sparse switch.

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical GC/1.3 lowers sparse outer cases 3, 4, 5, 6, and 12 as a binary-search tree, while retail dispatches through an owned 10-entry jump table and has three additional dispatch relocations.
MWCC 2.4.2 roots a switch binary-search tree at the median case and emits a bare branch without a compare for an empty case; a retail pivot below the lowest visible case exposed a hidden case -1.
lessons.workaround: Recover the hidden empty case from the median pivot and represent case -1 explicitly.

lessons.precise_divergence: MWCC's dense-switch jump tables are compiler-owned data in the function's translation unit; leaving them externalized in aggregate data prevents the complete object from matching and linking at the retail layout.
lessons.workaround: Name and assign each generated jump-table region to its owning translation unit, normalize the split object's data alignment where documented, and shrink the standalone auto-data object accordingly.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_8000A668, fn_8000EE9C, fn_8001E644, fn_80020E94, fn_80050730, and fn_8005EE9C

lessons.precise_divergence: MWCC-generated switch tables contain relocations to interior targets in their owning function, but those data bytes and relocations can be recovered exactly even while the function's code remains NonMatching or undecompiled.
lessons.workaround: Represent the documented table as honest-C interior function addresses in a standalone data translation unit, and do not assign matching code ownership to the function until its instruction stream independently passes the match gate.

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical GC/1.3 folds retail's equivalent lower-bound branch-plus-jump pairs or nested-switch branches into shorter inverted branches, producing eight fewer code bytes.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_80049818 and fn_8004998C

lessons.precise_divergence: Incomplete recovery of the source control flow leaves MWCC's generated switch layout or ownership different from retail: fn_80050B08 generates 5796 code bytes and 98 relocation-bearing instructions versus 5904 and 100 retail; fn_8005EF94's 100-byte switch table remains unmatched; and fn_800614A8's twelve irregular switches generate 6940 code bytes and 310 relocation-bearing instructions versus 6696 and 308 retail.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_80050B08, fn_8005EF94, and fn_800614A8

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical MWCC emits a signed- or unsigned-integer conversion bias as a compiler-private literal (often in sdata2), while retail relocates against an existing shared constant; code may otherwise be identical.
lessons.workaround: Externalize the conversion-bias constant to the retail symbol when its identity is known.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for every listed function

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical MWCC retains, permutes, or delays ordinary floating constants across calls and tests, whereas retail reloads them or schedules their loads earlier.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for every listed function

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical MWCC allocates the final signed-integer-to-double temporary in a fresh 0x10/0x14 stack slot, while retail reuses 0x8/0xC, producing four displacement differences.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_8000EB14 and fn_8000EBD4

lessons.precise_divergence: Canonical GC/1.3 uses different stack-slot reuse and has one differing four-byte move, producing an 804-byte function versus 800 bytes in retail; both objects still contain 43 relocation-bearing instructions with the same semantic targets.

Canonical GC/1.3 selects a stack frame 16 bytes different from retail: fn_80060F9C retains the exact 1292-byte code size despite that frame-allocation delta, while fn_8006330C uses 0x40 bytes where retail uses 0x50 despite its exact 2412-byte code size.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_80060F9C and fn_8006330C

lessons.precise_divergence: Unrecovered stack-local or aggregate layout changes canonical MWCC's frame and access pattern from retail, contributing to code-size and relocation-count differences in these large dispatchers.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_800614A8, fn_80063E64, and fn_800654F8

lessons.precise_divergence: Matching the float-heavy renderer requires the retail 0x60-byte frame, paired-single f31 save/restore, preserved float return lifetime, seven stack color values, and the float-leading variadic ABI.
lessons.workaround: Preserve those ABI-visible lifetimes and stack arguments in the source types and call expression.

lessons.precise_divergence: A 64-bit query result expressed as a direct cast does not reproduce retail's li -1; and lowering; an explicit truncation through 32 bits does.
lessons.workaround: Represent the return as 64-bit and explicitly truncate it through a 32-bit result.

lessons.precise_divergence: Natural C emits a 24-byte frame for the adjacent time-base arithmetic helpers, while retail uses a 32-byte ABI frame; __OSGetSystemTime remains a near-match and __OSTimeToSystemTime was promoted with the exact frame.
lessons.workaround: Use the documented transparent MWCC inline-assembly body when exact natural-C frame codegen is unavailable.
evidence: docs/matching.md: Small game continuation and OS time-base primitives

lessons.precise_divergence: Retail preserves multiple long-lived GPR or floating arguments across calls using an inline stmw/lmw prologue and epilogue selected by a translation-unit pragma.
lessons.workaround: Enable the TU-local use_lmw_stmw pragma and preserve the source-level argument lifetimes.

lessons.precise_divergence: An incomplete converter declaration does not record the recovered double argument passed to fn_800F5C54 and therefore does not express the retail call ABI precisely.
lessons.workaround: Declare fn_800F5C54 with its recovered double parameter.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_8001CB10 and fn_8001CB88

lessons.precise_divergence: The recovered 26-argument effect record and aggregate layout do not reproduce retail's call setup: canonical GC/1.3 emits 956 bytes and 70 relocation-bearing instructions versus 1028 bytes and 68 in retail.

Incomplete call-signature recovery changes generated argument setup and relocation materialization: fn_80063E64 emits 3440 bytes and 179 relocation-bearing instructions versus 3284 and 184 retail, while fn_800654F8 emits 4552 bytes versus 4700 and substitutes two additional SDA21 references for four retail absolute-address materializations.
evidence: reports/GEDE01/progress.json: open_items entries for fn_80063E64 and fn_800654F8

lessons.precise_divergence: Inlining the eight-byte maximum getter removes a retail call and therefore cannot match even though the operation is semantically equivalent.
lessons.workaround: Keep the maximum getter out of line.

lessons.precise_divergence: Repeated recovered source helpers remain out of line in canonical output, while retail's much larger main function indicates different inlining or recovered expression boundaries; generated size is 1108 bytes versus 2060 retail.
